correctness.rationale: The recurrence groups aligned triples as (a_m,1-a_m,a_m), a_m=x_{2m}; adjacent equalities in x can start only at indices 2 mod 3. Every four successive a_m include adjacent equal a-values because one of their even-index pairs equals x_(3j),x_(3j+2). An alternating x factor of length ten would cross three consecutive aligned triple boundaries, forcing four alternating a-values, a contradiction; maximum alternation length at most nine. In a period-p length-3p cube with 3 not dividing p, any equal neighboring letters recur at two or three pair starts with distinct residues mod3, impossible. The cube must therefore be alternating, requiring even p and 3p<=9, hence p=2, words 010101 or 101010. If L>=3p and p coprime to3, the alternating period-2 prefix propagates and L<=9; otherwise exponent below 3. Recurrence directly gives x12..20=101010101, attaining sharp 9/2. No assumption on periods divisible by three.
residual_risks: The theorem is for restricted periods 3 not dividing p only; unrestricted critical exponent is not determined.
